title: KMRD materials research data schema
description: Materials Research Data Schema (version 2026-01) developed by the Expert Committee for Materials R&D Data Standardization in the National Center of Materials Research Data (NCMRD) of Korea

dataset ID.$comment: this is required to exclusively identify the materials in this dataset. Partial data of the materials can be thus integrated into one complete dataset.
dataset ID.description: ID for dataset, automatically assigned by the KMDS data platform

dataset name.description: name of the data set, named by data provider; This is your own unique data or specimen identifier. With this text string alone, you should be able to identify the materials (system) in your own internal data management system.

data classification.description: classification code for relevant fields of science and technology announced by Ministry of Science and ICT of KOREA (https://www.law.go.kr)

data generation date.description: date when the data is added to the present database or data lake

data source.description: source information of the data, such as lab log, source publication, related projects, DOI of data, lead author, and publication date if the data is extracted from a publication; The DOI number referring to the published paper or dataset where the data can be found. If the data is unpublished, enter “Unpublished”; lead author is the surname of the first author. If several authors, end with et al. If the DOI number is given correctly, this will be extracted automatically from www.crossref.org ; publication date will be extracted automatically from www.crossref.org if the DOI number is given correctly.
examples: extracted from Acta Mater vol 13, page 2089 (2000)

name.description: contributor's name in the form of "[last name], [first name]"

position.description: Position or role of the contributor

affiliation.description: contributor's affiliation (institute's name and further description of working place)

researcher number.description: contributor’s researcher number ID in Integrated R&D Information System of Korea (https://iris.go.kr); only applied for Korean researchers

keywords.description: keywords representing the data set or material type and description, at least 3 keywords should be provided

embargo.description: date when allowing open access of the data

note on data.description: additional information or comments about the data
examples: Outlier removed due to device failure, initial measurement

materials.description: inherent data of material that composed of the material system; this is array of n materials defined by the material_id

id.description: id of materials inside of the dataset, that is to be used for defining materials system

universal specimen identifier.$comment: this is required to exclusively identify the materials in this dataset. Partial data of the materials can be thus integrated into one complete dataset.
universal specimen identifier.description: unique identifier of material specimen; automatically assigned as "dataset ID"-"material id"

name.description: description of materials according to customary usage, designation system, composition, supplier, brand name, polymer name based on IUPAC recommendation (https://iupac.org/polymer-edu/polymer-naming/), etc.

physicochemical information.description: physical and chemical information of material

composition.description: composition of materials

value.description: composition value in dictionary form; {"constituent": concentration,....}

unit.description: unit of the composition value in at.%, wt.% or mol.%

doping.description: dopant and its dose for modifying structure and properties of materials

level.description: doping level as the dose of each element in the form of dictionary {"dopant": dose in atom per square cm"}

dopant distribution map.description: URI of image file showing degree of uniformity of doping concentration distribution within a specimen

oxidation state.description: number of electrons that an atom is considered to have lost or gained relative to its neutral elemental state, assuming that all bonds are purely ionic; data in dictionary form {"constituent": "oxidation state",....}
oxidation state.alias: valence state; chemical state; oxidation number

density.description: mass per unit volume of a substance

pellet density.description: mass of compressed pellet of powder materials divided by the volume of the pellet

ligand exchange degree.description: Fraction of the initial surface ligands replaced by incoming ligands, reported on a clearly stated molar, site-occupancy, or spectroscopic basis
ligand exchange degree.alias: surface ligand exchange degree; ligand replacement degree

hybrid bonds.description: fraction of s-p hybrid bond in the materials. This fraction is dependent on the materials process and is significant in understanding materials structure and properties in covalent bonded materials composed of C, N, O, B, Be, P, or S

sp fraction.description: quantity of sp hybridization in percent; In chemistry, hybrid bonds are formed by hybridizing orbitals. sp hybrid bonds forms a linear geometry when one s orbital mixes with one p orbital forming two equivalent sp hybrid orbitals

sp2 fraction.description: quantity of sp2 hybridization in percent

sp3 fraction.description: quantity of sp3 hybridization in percent

molecule.description: molecules as the unit of materials; the smallest structural unit of a polymer that retains the chemical composition and connectivity of the repeating segments in the polymer chain

CAS number.description: a numeri(c)al designation assigned to chemical substances by the U.S. Chemical Abstracts Service (CAS)

chemical formula.description: molecular formula about the chemical proportions of atoms that constitute whole number ratio of atoms present in a compound or constitutional unit

formula weight.description: sum of the standard atomic weights of the constituent elements, each multiplied by its stoichiometric coefficient in the formula, expressed in grams per mole (g/mol)

SMILES.description: human-readable string notation for describing the structure of molecules, simplified molecular-input line-entry system

structural formula.description: molecular formula about a typographic system arose to describe organic structures in a line of functional group

plasticizer.description: a substance added to a material, typically a polymer, to make it softer, more flexible, and easier to handle. Plasticizers reduce intermolecular forces within the polymer matrix, decreasing the glass transition temperature and improving processability.

classification.description: 22 classifications based on the chemical structure of constitutional repeating unit of the polymer and related categories (Ref: https://polymer.nims.go.jp/PoLyInfo/guide/en/term_polymer.html)

degree of polymerization.description: number of each monomers contained in one polymer chain or polymer molecule; it is calculated for homopolymer by dividing the molecular weight of the polymer by the molecular weight of the repeat unit.

dispersity.description: ratio of the weight-average molecular weight to the number-average molecular weight; dispersity D = (M_w) / (M_n), where M_w is the weight-average molecular weight and M_n the number-average molecular weight
dispersity.alias: polydispersity index; PDI; molecular weight distribution

GPC (SEC) peak molar mass.description: molecular weight obtained from the peak value refers to the maximum point of gel permeation chromatographic (GPC) peak or size exclusion chromatographic (SEC) peak; the peak value provides the information about the molecular weight and distribution of polymers.

number-average molar mass.description: number-average molecular weights of materials; the average molecular weight of a polymer sample based on the number of molecules; M_n = sum{(N_i) x (M_i)} / sum {(N_i)}, where N_i is the number of molecules of species i and M_i the molecular weight of species i.

viscosity-average molar mass.description: a measure to characterize the molecular weight of a polymer based on its viscosity; particularly useful for understanding the flow behavior of polymer solutions and melts; M_v = K x [eta], where K is a constant that depends on the specific polymer and solvent used and [eta] the intrinsic viscosity of the polymer solution, which is a measure of how the viscosity of a solution changes with concentration.

weight-average molar mass.description: weight-average molecular weights of materials; a measure of the average molecular weight of a polymer sample, taking into account the weight of each molecule; M_w = sum{(w_i) x (M_i)} / sum{(w_i)}, where w_i is the weight of species i and M_i the molecular weight of species i

z-average molar mass.description: average molecular weight that gives greater weight to larger molecules, making it particularly sensitive to high molecular weight species within the distribution; M_z= sum{(M_i)^2 x (N_i)} / sum{(M_i) x (N_i)}, where M_i is the molecular weight of species i and N_i the number of molecules of species i

architecture.description: molecular structure regarding atom connectivity and arrangement; structural information when the polymer chain is seen within the range that is bigger than the constitutional repeating unit
architecture.alias: molecular structure; molecular arrangement; chain architecture

homogeneity.description: monomer homogeneity of the polymer chain

end groups.description: chemical group or functional group present at the two ends of a polymer chain, which significantly influence the reactivity, properties and degradation of the polymer

branch molecule.description: a molecular branch or chain connected to the main polymer backbone; a molecular chain that extends from the main polymer backbone chain; it is a deviation from a perfectly linear structure.

number of branches.description: average number of branches attached to a single polymer molecule

degree of branching.description: percentage of the number of branches present in a polymer in its total number of repeating units

average branch length.description: length of the polymer chains between branching points

branching density.description: number of branches per unit length of the main polymer chain

branching index.description: ratio between the radius of gyration of a branched polymer and that of a linear polymer of the same molar mass (range : 0~1)

cross-linking density.description: number of cross-links per unit volume in a polymer network, representing the degree of interconnection between polymer chains through chemical bonds. It quantifies the three-dimensional network structure formed when polymer chains are linked together by covalent or ionic bonds.
cross-linking density.alias: network density; degree of cross-linking; cross-link density

cross-linking agent.description: A substance that promotes or regulates the formation of covalent bonds between polymer chains, resulting in a three-dimensional network structure. These agents react with functional groups on the polymer chains to create bridges or cross-links that connect separate polymer molecules.
cross-linking agent.alias: cross-linker; curing agent; hardener; vulcanizing agent; cross-linking additive; reticulating agent
examples: Epoxy hardeners (amine or anhydride-based curing agents)
Ethylene glycol dimethacrylate (EGDMA - crosslinking of methacrylate polymers)

core.description: central part of star polymer that acts as the central junction point from which all the polymer arms radiate outwards

arm number.description: number of linear polymer chains that radiate from the central core

arm length.description: length of each individual polymer arm

number of generation.description: total number of generation to indicate the level of branching in a dendrimer. It starts from generation 0 (the core) and increases with each layer of branching

core.description: central part of star polymer that acts as the central junction point from which all the polymer arms radiate outwards

branches.description: average number and length of branches in each generation

length.description: average length of branches in each generation

degree of ladderization.description: fraction (or percentage) of the polymer backbone that has successfully formed the complete double-stranded ladder structure via cyclization reaction, without open-chain defects

persistence length.description: A measure of the stiffness of a polymer chain, defined as the length over which the direction of the polymer backbone segments remains correlated (i.e., the chain behaves like a rigid rod)

dihedral angle.description: angle between planes defined by the backbone atoms, quantifying the twist or contortion of the ladder structure. It determines the planarity of the ribbon-like chain

fractional free volume.description: ratio of the specific free volume (empty space not occupied by the polymer chains) to the total specific volume of the polymer material; FFV=(V_sp-1.34V_vdw)/V_sp

name.description: conventional name of backbone molecule of the bottlebrush polymer

degree of polymerization.description: number of repeating units in the backbone

dispersity.description: dispersity of backbone; ratio of the weight-average molecular weight to the number-average molecular weight
dispersity.alias: polydispersity index; PDI; molecular weight distribution

degree of polymerization.description: number of each monomers contained in one polymer chain or polymer molecule; it is calculated for homopolymer by dividing the molecular weight of the polymer by the molecular weight of the repeat unit.

dispersity.description: dispersity of side chain; ratio of the weight-average molecular weight to the number-average molecular weight;

grafting density.description: number of side chains per backbone repeat unit

composition.description: molar percent of each comonomer type in a copolymer chain in dictionary form {"monomer": "mol. %",...}

model.description: information of the computation model in the case of computation or simulation data

box dimension.description: dimension parameters of the simulation box. Cubic simulation box is assumed if the angles are not defined.

elements.description: data of elements in the simulation model

symbol.description: symbol of the element consisting in the box

number.description: number of element in the box

phase.description: major state of the model or major crystal structure when the model is solid

structure file.description: URI of structure file used for computation or simulation. File format is determined by extension of the file name

adsorbate.description: substance that is adsorbed by another material

surface model.description: characteristics of the material's surface at the atomic or molecular level for calculation

Miller index.description: orientation of the crystal plane along which the bulk material is "cut" to create a surface or slab model

termination.description: specific atomic configuration or arrangement at the exposed surface of the slab model

chemical potential.description: chemical potential values of constituent elements in the slab/gas model for computing surface energy in dictionary form of {"element":"chemical potential in eV", ...}

slab thickness.description: atomic layer thickness of slab model

vacuum thickness.description: vacuum layer thickness of slab model

defect model.description: characteristics of defects that exist in the material

cell optimization.description: TRUE if the simulation cell lattice parameters are optimized

finite-size supercell correction.description: A set of post-processing corrections applied to DFT total energies of charged defects in periodic supercell models to remove artificial electrostatic interactions between a defect and its periodic images, elastic image interactions, and band filling errors arising from the finite size of the supercell
finite-size supercell correction.alias: finite-size correction; image charge correction; supercell correction; electrostatic correction

correction scheme.description: Name of the finite-size correction scheme applied to the charged defect supercell calculation

supercell size.description: Number of primitive unit cells contained in the supercell used for the defect calculation

supercell lattice parameter.description: Lattice parameter of the supercell along the principal axis, determining the minimum defect-image distance

defect charge state.description: Formal charge state of the defect introduced into the supercell, used to determine the magnitude of electrostatic correction

static dielectric constant.description: Static (ionic + electronic) dielectric constant of the host material used in the electrostatic correction, accounting for full dielectric screening of the defect charge

electronic dielectric constant.description: High-frequency (electronic) dielectric constant of the host material, corresponding to the optical dielectric response without ionic contribution

dielectric tensor.description: Full 3×3 dielectric tensor of the host material used in anisotropic correction schemes such as Kumagai-Oba, required for non-cubic crystal systems

Madelung constant.description: Madelung constant of the supercell lattice geometry used in Makov-Payne and Lany-Zunger correction schemes

potential alignment.description: Electrostatic potential alignment term between the defect supercell and the perfect host supercell, evaluated at regions far from the defect where the perturbation has decayed to zero
potential alignment.alias: ΔV; alignment correction; long-range potential offset

electrostatic correction energy.description: Total electrostatic energy correction applied to the charged defect formation energy to remove artificial periodic image interactions

band filling correction energy.description: Energy correction applied to remove the artificial band filling error arising from the occupation of conduction band states by electrons introduced with shallow donor defects in finite supercells

band gap correction.description: Correction applied to the DFT-calculated band gap to account for the systematic underestimation by LDA or GGA functionals, used to correctly position defect transition levels within the band gap
band gap correction.alias: band gap error correction; scissor correction

correction software.description: Name and version of the software package used to compute and apply the finite-size supercell correction

corrected defect formation energy.description: Final defect formation energy after application of all finite-size corrections, used to determine defect thermodynamics and charge transition levels

structure.description: structural information of materials in all scales; crystallographic, micro, meso and macro scales

DOS.description: proportion of states that are to be occupied by the system at each energy, submitted in the form of file or array number data

DOS data.alias: density of states data, DOS data

density of state.description: density of the state corresponding to the energy

DOS file.description: URI of the numeral array file of the density of state

band gap.description: energy range in a solid where no electronic states can exist (between valence band maximum and conduction band minimum)

bowing parameter.description: A parameter that describes nonlinear variation of band gap between two materials with different lattice constants

energy.description: numerical value of the band gap energy

value.description: numerical value of the band gap energy

type.alias: gap type; optical gap type, transition type

graded.description: TRUE if the band gap varies as a function of the vertical position of the materials i.e. in the perovskite layer.

valence band maximum.description: highest energy point within the valence band that is occupied by electrons at absolute zero temperature

conduction band minimum.description: lowest energy point within the conduction band that is the range of unoccupied electronic states above the valence band

band edge reference.description: Energy reference level with respect to which the valence band maximum and conduction band minimum are reported

Fermi level.description: thermodynamic work required to add one electron to the body

electron density profile.description: URI of the electron density profile image file; three-dimensional voxel-based representation of electron density within a material. The data encodes the spatial distribution of electron density across a discretized grid, where each voxel corresponds to an electron density value at a specific position in real space.

crystallinity.description: fraction (percentage) of a material that is crystalline (as opposed to amorphous)

lattice parameter.description: Lattice parameters of the lattice according to the convention described in web.archive.org. The unit cell is the basic building block of a crystal, repeated infinitely in three dimensions. It is characterized by: three vectors (a, b, c) that form the edges of a parallelepiped; the angles between the vectors (alpha, the angle between b and c; beta, the angle between a and c; gamma, the angle between a and b). Depending on the crystal system, there are sometimes restrictions on the values that unit cell parameters can take.

unit cell.description: smallest portion of a crystal lattice that shows the three-dimensional pattern of the entire crystal

cell volume.description: three-dimensional space occupied by one unit cell in a crystal lattice

Z.description: number of formula units of a substance contained within one unit cell of its crystal lattice

density of crystal structure.description: mass of the atoms within a unit cell divided by the volume of the unit cell

strukturbericht designation.description: crystal structure classification system established by the Zeitschrift für Kristallographie

space group.description: space group name or number of the structure

extinction symbol.description: symbol represents specific systematic absences in a crystal's diffraction pattern

full width at half maximum of XRC.description: Full width at half maximum of the rocking curve peak, used as a primary indicator of crystalline quality; smaller values indicate higher crystal perfection
full width at half maximum of XRC.alias: peak width; rocking curve width; omega FWHM

polytype.description: Crystalline solids that have the same molecular structure but exhibit changes in crystal structure due to variations in packing and molecular arrangement

Lotgering factor.description: A measurement to assess the crystallographic orientations of inorganic bulk materials. Typically calculated based on the intensities measured using X-raydiffraction pattern data. This factor serves as a convenient orientation index for determining the degree of crystallographic alignment in materials. Defined as (P-Po)/(1-Po) where P and Po are the intensity ratios for the sample and randomly oriented sample, respectively.

microstructure.description: microstructural features of materials including phase, morphology, and texture

phase.description: information of phases in a material

id.description: id of phase for internal use of the dataset, that would be used for defining materials structure

name.description: name of a phase according to its thermodynamic state and/or crystal structure

role.description: role of the phase in the materials

composition.description: composition of the phase

value.description: composition value in dictionary form; {"constituent": concentration,....}

unit.description: unit of the composition value in at.%, wt.% or mol.%

fraction.description: relative amounts of the phase in the microstructure
fraction.alias: phase amounts, volume fraction of phases

grain.description: microstructural characteristics of grain when this phase acts as matrix grain

grain size.description: estimate of the average grain diameter

aspect ratio.description: length ratio between longest distance and shortest distance of grain

recrystallization fraction.description: fraction of the microstructure that consists of recrystallized grains

kernel average misorientation.description: average misorientation angle between each measuring point (kernel) and its neighboring points in EBSD data, used to assess local lattice distortion

size.description: characteristic size of precipitates determined using a specified size measurement or calculation method

length.description: average length of precipitate phase; typically the longest dimension of rod- or plate-shaped particles

diameter.description: average diameter of spherical or rod-shaped precipitate

aspect ratio.description: length ratio between longest distance and shortest distance of precipitate

solute concentration.description: concentration of solute atoms in a specific phase, typically expressed in atomic percent (at.%)

nucleation site.description: location (microstructural feature) where the precipitate initially forms

texture table.description: relative probability of finding the crystals comprising a polycrystalline aggregate in various orientations

texture component.description: specific orientation distribution as a measure for the strength and scatter of a crystallographic texture

fraction.description: fraction of a specific orientation distribution as a measure for the strength and scatter of a crystallographic texture

pole figure.description: graphical representation of the orientation of texture components

inverse pole figure.description: A plot showing the distribution of sample directions in the reference frame of a crystal.

ODF section plot.description: URI of graphical representation of the Orientation Distribution Function (ODF)

maximum intensity plane.description: crystal plane with the highest intensity in the pole figure or texture data

maximum intensity.description: maximum multiple of random distribution (MRD) value observed in a texture measurement

Schmid factor plane.description: slip plane on which the Schmid factor is calculated

Schmid factor axis.description: slip direction used in the Schmid factor calculation

Schmid factor.description: ratio of resolved shear stress to applied stress, representing the geometric projection onto a slip system

morphology.description: morphological data of materials of various shapes;
morphology.$comment: Mathematically all materials are of 3D morphology, but materials morphologies can be divided conventionally into 4 classes 0D, 1D, 2D, 3D and hybrid/hierarchical ones; 0D materials has small and similar dimenion in all directions, 1D materials has small dimensions in two directions but large dimension in one direction, 2D materials has small dimensions in one direction but large dimensions in other two directions, 3D materials has large dimensions in all three directions. hybrid/hierarchical materials has multiple dimensions that cannot be expressed in one kind of morphological parameters.

0D.description: data for materials of 0D morphology; octahdron particle, shperical particles

shape.description: name of 0D materials shape in conventional way

sphericity.description: ratio of the surface area of a sphere with the same volume as the particle to the actual surface area of the particle

aspect ratio.description: ratio of a particle's longest dimension to its shortest dimension

elongation.description:
he extent to which an object is stretched along its major axis; often calculated as 
 1−(𝑏/𝑎), where 𝑎 and 𝑏 are major and minor axes

diameter.description: average diameter of spherical or rod shaped particles; equivalent diameter of particle with comlicated shape that can be obtained by the diameter of a sphere that have the same volume of the particle

x.description: dimension in x direction of plate shaped particles

y.description: dimension in y direction of plate shaped particles

z.description: dimension in z direction of rectangular shaped particles

facet surface.description: array of facet surface indexes of particle

1D.description: data for materials of 1d morphology; bar, wire, tubes

shape.description: name of 1D materials shape in conventional way

base dimension.description: dimension of rectangular or square shape bases of 1D material

x.description: length of rectangular base in x-direction

y.description: length of rectangular base in y-direction

inner diameter.description: inner diameter of the tube or cylinder shape 1D material

outer diameter.description: outer diameter of the tube or cylinder shape 1D material

orientation.description: orientation in the direction of length

aspect ratio.description: ratio of the major axis length to the minor axis length

2D.description: data for materials of 2D morphology; thin film, nano sheet, disk, plate

note.description: description of essential characteristics of 2D structure

projected area.description: area enclosed by a 2D material's projected outline; used for estimate the effective diameter
projected area.alias: cross-sectional area; apparent area; TEM projected area

perimeter.description: total boundary length of 2D material projection or cross-section

feret diameter.description: distance between two parallel tangents on opposite sides of a material's projection; varies with measurement direction

dimension.description: dimension of the plate in the form of xyt

thickness.description: distance between two wide sides of 2D material

curvature.description: rate of change of the tangetn angle along a curved surface

roughness.description: deviation of a surface from its ideeal plane, expressed by average rouchness Ra

substrate.description: materials of the substrate

wrinkle density.description: number of wrinkles, folds, or ridge features per unit area on a surface

x.description: length in x-direction of rectangular bulk material

y.description: length in y-direction of rectangular bulk material

z.description: length in z-direction of rectangular bulk material

diameter.description: equivalent diameter in spherical bulk; approximate value of the equivalent diameter of 3D bulk material of spherical but irregular shape.

cluster size.description: average or maximum dimension of aggregated particles or connected domains

solution.description: single phase material where a solute dissolves in a suitable solvent. ex) Polymer chains are dispersed throughout the solvent, which can be liquid or gas

solute.description: material ID or name of solute

solvent.description: medium in which the solute dissolves.

pore diameter.description: size of the pores in material; in some cases, pores can have multiple number of distinguishable sizes

average pore diameter.description: mean diameter of pores (or voids) present in a given material

pore limiting diameter.description: diameter of the largest probe that can traverse through pore channels

pore fraction.description: fraction of a material's volume that is empty

defect.description: defect of materials ranging from 0D point defects to 2D interface

0D defect.description: defects that occur only at or around a single lattice point

species.description: a specific chemical species (element or molecule) constituting a point defect in the material

formation energy.description: defect formation energy, i.e. lattice cohesive energy in the case of vacancy

density.description: ratio of defected lattice sites to those containing atoms

electric charge.description: charge state of point defects in the unit of electron

1D defect.description: linear crystallographic defect or irregularity within a crystal structure which contains an abrupt change in the arrangement of atoms

enum: micropipe (large size defects formed and observed along the C-axis)

Burgers vector.description: magnitude and direction of the lattice distortion resulting from a dislocation

defect generation depth.description: vertical distance from the surface or interface to the point where the defect originated

density.description: measure of the number of dislocations in a unit volume of a crystalline material

velocity.description: velocity of mobile dislocation upon applied stress

2D defect.description: planar defect separating two phases or crystal lattices, each of which may be solid, liquid, or gaseous

coherency.description: degree of right alignment of atoms across boundaries (2D defect)

interfacial energy.description: energy required to form a unit area of new interface

misorientation.description: difference in crystallographic orientation between two crystallites in a polycrystalline material

misfit strain.description: strain induced at the interface between two materials or phases due to a mismatch in their lattice parameters.

3D defect.description: volumetric defect such as void, pores, or clusters in the materials, which is unintentionally incorporated in the materials.

volume fraction.description: volume fraction of the 3D defect with respect to the volume of whole materials

fraction.description: fraction of defect of the corresponding size

composition.description: composition value in dictionary form; {"constituent": concentration,....}

unit.description: unit of the composition value in at.%, wt.% or mol.%

interface.description: interfacial properties between phases or materials

lattice misfit.description: difference in lattice parameters between two crystalline phases

associated phases.description: variable names of the two phases associated with the misfit value

specific area.description: specific surface area of material per unit mass

electrochemically active surface area.description: electrochemically active surface area (ECSA) of material_n

curvature.description: rate of change of the tangetn angle along a curved surface

composition.description: quantitative description of the constituent elements, compounds, or phases present in a material or its surface layer, expressed as atomic percent (at.%)

value.description: composition value in dictionary form; {"constituent": concentration,....}

crystallography.description: arrangement of atoms at the outermost layers of a solid material. It describes the geometric configuration, including the positions of atoms relative to each other, the presence of defects (like vacancies or adatoms), and the overall symmetry of the surface.

Miller indices.description: direction of surface normal in Miller indices; Miller indices is the notation in crystallography to describe the orientation of crystal planes and directions in a crystal lattice

unit cell.description: smallest repeating unit of a crystal structure at the surface of a material

polymeric structure.description: structural properties specific to polymer materials

polymer blend type.description: a classification of polymer blends according to the morphology and phase distribution of the constituent polymers
polymer blend type.alias: polymer blend morphology; polymer blend phase separation

free volume.description: Unoccupied or void space within a polymer matrix that is not directly occupied by polymer chains or atoms. It represents the difference between the total volume of the polymer and the volume physically occupied by its constituent molecules. Free volume strongly affects diffusion, permeability, glass transition behavior, and mechanical relaxation in polymers.
free volume.alias: free space; molecular void; unoccupied volume

polymer cross-link.description: crosslink density obtained by Flory-Rehner equation using the swelling ratio

cross-link density.description: density value; result of Flory-Rehner equation

swelling ratio.description: value of swelling ratio defined by the ratio of the volume or mass of swollen polymer network in equilibrium with solvent to that of dry polymer

raw analysis data.description: URI of materials analysis data file obtained by microscopic observation, instrumental analysis or computation and simulation;

property.description: attribute, quality, or characteristic of materials

biomedical property.description: properties that characterize the interaction and performance of materials in biological and medical applications

antibacterial property.description: ability of materials to inhibit or kill microorganisms

minimum inhibitory concentration (MIC).description: minimum concentration to inhibit microbial growth

zone of inhibition.description: area where antibacterial substances (such as antibiotics, antimicrobials) have an inhibitory effect on microbial growth

antibacterial efficiency.description: ability of materials or antibacterial agent to inhibit the growth and multiplication of bacteria

biocompatibility.description: properties that characterize the compatibility between materials and biological systems

cytotoxicity.description: level of toxicity on cells (measured by IC50, cell viability % etc.)

inflammatory response.description: body’s response to injury (ex: cytokine, TNF-α, IL-6 level etc.)

hemocompatibility.description: core performance indicators of materials applied in the blood environment (platlet adhesion amount)

bioactivity.description: ability of materials to induce specific biological responses

osteointegration.description: ability of the materials to form a direct bond with bone tissue

surface reactivity.description: ability of the material surface to interact with the cell

biodegradability.description: ability of materials to be gradually broken down, absorbed or metabolized in an organism

degradation rate.description: rate of decomposition of materials in the biological environment

degradation product.description: substances generated by the decomposition of a material, assessed in terms of their concentration and potential harmful effects on living organism

cytocompatibility.description: ability of the materials to support cell attachment, proliferation and differentiation

cell adhesion rate.description: ability of cells to adhere to the surface of the materials

cell proliferation rate.description: rate of cell growth on the surface of the materials

cell differentiation.description: whether the material supports cell differentiation to specific functional cells

immune compatibility.description: ability to avoid adverse immune responses

immune cell activation.description: cells in the immune system undergo a series of physiological and functional changes after being stimulated by specific signals

complement activation.description: defense mechanisms that help the body recognizes, attacks, and eliminates pathogens

osteogenic property.description: ability of the materials to promote bone tissue formation and repair

mineralized nodule formation.description: assessment of mineralization by alizarin red staining

tissue compatibility.description: compatibility of the materials with specific tissues (e.g. bone, cartilage, skin)

tissue integration.description: degree of bonding of the materials to the surrounding tissue

tissue regeneration.description: process by which tissues or organs recover the structure and function after injury or damage through cell proliferation and differentiation

chemical property.description: characteristics of a material associated with changes in chemical state

adsorption.description: characteristics of the interaction between adsorbate and substrate

adsorbate type.description: name of adsorbed atom or molecule

initial adsorption site.description: type of adsorption site of the adsorbate before structural relaxation

initial adsorption orientation.description: orientation of the adsorbate before structural relaxation

relaxed adsorption site.description: type of adsorption site of the adsorbate after structural relaxation
relaxed adsorption site.alias: optimized adsorption site, optimized binding site

relaxed adsorption orientation.description: orientation of adsorbed guest molecule (or atom) after relaxation

direction vector.description: direction vector connecting atom labels of starting and end point of the vector in the form of dictionary {"starting atom label":"ending atom label"}

adsorption energy.description: energy change associated with the process of a guest molecule (or atom) attaching to the surface or internal sites of a host material (based on total energy difference, no further thermal correction)

shortest binding distance.description: shortest distance between adsorbed guest molecule (or atom) and slab surface atom

atom labels.description: atom labels related to the shortest distance in dictionary form of {"atom label in the absobate":"atom label in the slab"}

distance.description: shortest interatomic distance between the adsorbate and the atoms of the slab surface

dissociative adsorption.description: TRUE if the adsorbate is dissociated after adsorption

energy per atom.description: total energy divided by the number of atoms

ion exchange capacity.description: measure of a material's ability to exchange ions with its surrounding environment, expressed in equivalents per gram or per milliliter

corrosion property.description: properties related to deterioration of a material as it reacts with its environment via electrochemical and chemical reactions

anodic partial current.description: sum of all the currents corresponding to anodic reactions on the electrode

cathodic partial current.description: sum of all the currents corresponding to cathodic electrochemical reactions on the electrode

corrosion current.description: anodic partial current due to metal oxidation

corrosion induced porosity.description: porosity induced by corrosion; porosity is defined as ratio of the volume of voids (empty spaces) within a material to the total volume of the material, which is used to describe the degree of emptiness or the amount of pores in a substance.

corrosion potential.description: electrode potential of a metal in a given corrosion system

corrosion rate.description: amount of corrosion loss per year in thickness

free corrosion current.description: corrosion current at the free corrosion potential

free corrosion potential.description: corrosion potential in the absence of net (external) electrical current flowing to or from the metal surface; The potential is measured with respect to the potential of the reference electrode.

mass loss rate.description: mass loss rate of the material by corrosion, converted to grams per area per year

passivation current.description: corrosion current at the passivation potential

passivation potential.description: corrosion potential, at which the corrosion current has a peak value, and above which there is a range of potentials, where the metal is in a passive state; The potential is measured with respect to the potential of the reference electrode.

pitting initiation potential.description: lowest value of the corrosion potential at which pit initiation is possible on a passive surface in a given corrosive environment; The potential is measured with respect to the potential of the reference electrode.

polarized potential.description: potential across the electrode/electrolyte interface that is the sum of the corrosion potential and the applied polarization

polarization resistance.description: resistance of a material or electrode to changes in its electrochemical potential when a small current is applied. It reflects how easily the material can resist corrosion or chemical changes at its surface.

reactivation potential.description: corrosion potential below which reactivation takes place; The potential is measured with respect to the potential of the reference electrode.

redox potential.description: potential of a reversible oxidation-reduction reaction in a given electrolyte recorded on a S.H.E. scale

standard electrode potential.description: reversible potential for an electrode process when all products and reactants are at unit activity, recorded on a S.H.E scale.

transpassivation potential.description: corrosion potential above which the metal is in the transpassive state; The potential is measured with respect to the potential of the reference electrode.

electrical property.description: physical properties that a material exhibits upon the application of electric forces

carrier type.description: type of charge carrier in a material (e.g., electron or hole)

carrier concentration.description: number of charge carriers per volume

carrier diffusion length.description: an average distance that the excess carriers can cover before they recombine

carrier lifetime.description: an average time it takes for a minority carrier to recombine

conduction band minimum.description: lowest range of vacant electronic states.
conduction band minimum.alias: CBM, LUMO, lowest unoccupied molecular orbital

value.description: data value in dictionary form; {"constituent": charge value,...}

critical temperature.description: temperature above which certain materials lose their permanent polarization properties

current density.description: amount of charge per unit time that flows through a unit area of a chosen cross section at an applied voltage

value.description: value of current density at an applied voltage

defect energy level.description: energy level of the states introduced within the band gap of a semiconductor or insulator due to the presence of defects

dielectric constant.description: relative permittivity compared to the vacuum in induced polarization stored in a material under electric field.

dielectric strength.description: maximum electric field that the material can withstand under ideal conditions without undergoing electrical breakdown and becoming electrically conductive

electric susceptibility.description: a dimensionless proportionality constant that indicates the degree of polarization of a material

electrical conductivity.description: quantity how strongly it conducts electric current

electron affinity.description: amount of energy released when an atom, molecule, or material gains an electron in the gas phase

electron effective mass.description: a mass that a particle seems to have when responding to forces or interacting with other identical particles in a thermal distribution

electron mobility.description: a value that represents how quickly a single electron can move through a metal or semiconductor, when pulled by an electric field

exciton binding energy.description: a binding energy of an exciton (an electrically neutral quasiparticle that exists in insulators or semiconductors)

Hall coefficient.description: ratio of the induced electric field to the product of the current density and the applied magnetic field

Hall voltage.description: Voltage difference across an electrical conductor that is transverse to an electric current in the conductor and to an applied magnetic field perpendicular to the current

hole effective mass.description: a mass that a particle seems to have when responding to forces or interacting with other identical particles in a thermal distribution

hole mobility.description: a value that represents how quickly a single hole can move through a metal or semiconductor, when pulled by an electric field

impedance.description: complex, frequency-dependent opposition a circuit presents to an alternating voltage/current, defined as the ratio of the phasor voltage to phasor current; the total opposition that a circuit presents to an alternating current or voltage, including both resistance and reactance

ionic conductivity.description: quantity how strongly it conducts ionic charge

ionic mobility.description: proportionality factor between an ion's drift velocity in an electric field in a specified medium

ionization energy.description: minimum energy required to remove an electron from a neutral atom or molecule in the gas phase, producing a positively charged ion

loss tangent.description: signal loss due to the dielectric materials' inherent dissipation of electromagnetic energy. It is dependent on the frequency of applied electric field.

permittivity.description: measure of the electric polarizability of a material

resistivity.description: quantity how strongly it resists electric current

bulk resistivity.description: intrinsic electrical resistivity of the material measured through its volume, expressed in ohms meter

surface resistivity.description: electrical resistance to current flow along the surface of the material, typically expressed in ohms per square

distribution map.description: URI of lateral distribution map of resistivity

spin-Hall angle.description: When a current is applied to a material with a very large spin-orbit interaction, the current does not go straight due to the strong spin-orbit interaction, and different spins diverge in the width direction on both sides of the sample, resulting in spin accumulation and spin current. The ratio of the generated spin current to the flowed current.

spin-orbit splitting energy.description: energy level splitting energy produced by the spin–orbit interaction of a particle's spin with its motion inside a potential

trap density.description: density of electronic trap states within dielectric materials responsible for carrier trapping and de-trapping

temperature coefficient of resistance.description: a change in resistance per unit resistance per degree rise in temperature based upon the resistance of 0 degree Celsius

valence band maximum.description: highest range of electron energies in which electrons are normally present at absolute zero temperature
valence band maximum.alias: VBM, HOMO, highest occupied molecular orbital

electrochemical property.description: property either caused or accompanied by the passage of an electric current

oxidation potential.description: oxidation potential (voltage vs. Li/Li+) of solid or liquid materials (e.g. the solvent, the conductive salt or solid electrolytes)

reduction potential.description: reduction potential (voltage vs. Li/Li+) of solid or liquid materials (e.g. the solvent, the conductive salt or solid electrolytes)

ferroelectric property.description: property of certain materials to have a spontaneous polarization which can be reversed by the application of an external electric field

coercive electric field.description: strength of the electric field at which the macroscopic polarization of the ferroelectric capacitor disappears, presented by values assigned to symbols E_{c}

remanent polarization.description: polarization that remains after removing the electric field applied to an object, presented by values assigned to symbols P_{r}

saturation polarization.description: Maximum polarization when an electric field is applied to an object, presented by values assigned to symbols P_{s}

negative remanent polarization.description: amount of polarization being negative region of hysteresis loop that remains in a material after an electric field is removed

positive remanent polarization.description: amount of polarization being positive region of hysteresis loop that remains in a material after an electric field is removed

polarization.description: total electric dipole moment per unit cell of a material

domain size.description: size of a region in a material that exhibits uniform polarization direction in ferroelectric materials

domain structure.$comment: structure of ferroelectric domains in PFM or TEM images

coercive voltage.description: voltage required to change polarization direction of ferroelectric materials

negative coercive voltage.description: negative voltage required to change polarization direction of ferroelectric materials

positive coercive voltage.description: positive voltage required to change polarization direction of ferroelectric materials

difference of coercive voltage.description: voltage difference between the positive and negative coercive voltages in the hysteresis loop

imprint field.description: field difference between coercive field value, presented by values assigned to symbols (|Ec+| - |Ec-|)/2

Born effective charge.description: second-order tensor that quantifies how the electric polarization in a crystal change in response to the displacement of an atom

gas transmission property.description: gas transmission property through the encapsulation materials
gas transmission property.alias: moisture transmission; air transmission; hydrogen permeability; gas permeation property

gas.description: chemical species of gas used for the permeability or transmission measurement

transmission rate.description: rate at which a gas or vapor passes through a material, influenced by diffusion and solubility characteristics; In general, permeability of a gas is defined as the volume of the gas that passes through a materials of a unit thickness per unit area and unit time, under a unit partial-pressure difference
transmission rate.alias: permeation rate; permeability; GTR; permeability rate

magnetic property.description: physical properties that a material exhibits upon the application of magnetic forces

absorption shielding effectiveness.description: amount of the attenuated amplitude of electromagnetic waves in the material, compared to the amount of the transmitted electromagnetic waves into the material

coercivity.description: magnetic field required to reduce the magnetic flux of a material to zero

Curie temperature.description: temperature above which certain materials lose their permanent magnetic properties

DMI energy density.description: Anti-symmetric exchange interaction that favors a canted spin configuration between neighboring spins
DMI energy density.alias: D, Dzyaloshinskii-Moriya interaction energy density, DMI constant, antisymmetric exchange energy constant, Dzyaloshinskii–Moriya interaction constant

DMI field.description: An effective in-plane magnetic field acting on a domain wall which tends to align the domain wall magnetization to the Neel configuration with a specific chirality

domain wall propagation field.description: minimum magnetic field required to move or propagate a domain wall within a ferromagnetic material

effective magnetic anisotropy energy.description: Net perpendicular magnetic anisotropy which is derived from the first-order uniaxial anisotropy constant (Ku) by eliminating shape anisotropy term (2πMs2)

interface state density.description: number of states per unit area of the interface per unit energy in the semiconductor band gap

intrinsic coercivity.description: magnetic field required to reduce the magnetization of a material to zero

magnetic anisotropy constant.description: A measure of the energy necessary to align the magnetization from an easy axis to the hard axis of the specimen. The easy and hard axis is determined by crystal structure, interface and the shape of the specimen.
magnetic anisotropy constant.alias: magnetic anisotropy energy; anisotropy energy constant

magnetic anisotropy energy.description: Energy required to rotate the magnetization from an easy axis to a hard axis

magnetic anisotropy field.description: Magnetic field required for complete magnetization in the direction in which the largest magnetic field is required for magnetization in a magnetic material having magentic anisotropy

magnetic field strength.alias: magnetic flux density, magnetic induction, magnetic intensity

magnetic induction.description: magnitude of the internal field strength (B) within a substance that is subjected to an externally applied magnetic field (H)

magneto-optical Kerr angle.description: Degree of ferromagnetic ordering of materials along with applied magnetic field direction, represented by the rotation angle of reflected light polarization when the light is reflected from the surface of a magnetized material

magnetization.description: In the presence of an externally applied magnetic field (H), the magnetic moments within a material tend to become aligned with the field and to reinforce it by virtue of their magnetic fields

magnetostriction.description: strain induced by a change in magnetization

maximum BH product.description: product of the magnetic flux density and magnetic field strength of a permanent magnet at any point of any demagnetization curve.

permeability.description: degree of magnetization of a material in response to a magnetic field

Neel temperature.description: temperature at which an antiferromagnetic material transitions to a paramagnetic state, meaning that thermal energy overcomes the exchange interactions maintaining the antiferromagnetic ordering.

recoil permeability.description: permeability corresponding to the slope of the recoil line

reflection shielding effectiveness.description: amount of the reflected electromagnetic waves from the material

relative permeability.description: relative permeability is the ratio of the permeability of a specific medium to the permeability of vacuum

remanent coercivity.description: magnetic field required to reduce the remanent magnetization of a material to zero, meaning that when the H field is finally returned to zero, then both B and M also fall to zero (the material reaches the origin in the hysteresis curve)

remanent flux density.description: value of the magnetic flux density remaining in a magnetized body when, in the absence of a self-demagnetizing field, the applied magnetic field strength is brought to zero

remanent magnetic polarization.description: value of the magnetic polarization remaining in a magnetized body when, in the absence of a self-demagnetizing field, the applied magnetic field strength is brought to zero

remanent magnetization.description: value of the magnetization remaining in a magnetized body when, in the absence of a self-demagnetizing field, the applied magnetic field strength is brought to zero

saturation flux density.description: maximum magnetic induction (Bs) that results when all the magnetic dipoles in a solid piece are mutually aligned with the external field (H). A state reached when an increase in applied external magnetic field H cannot increase the magnetization (M) of the material further.

saturation magnetic polarization.description: maximum obtainable magnetic polarization for a given substance at a given temperature

saturation magnetization.description: maximum obtainable magnetization for a given substance at a given temperature

spin Hall angle.description: conversion efficiency of the charge currents to pure spin currents

spin-orbit torque efficiency.description: conversion factor of the current density to the spin-orbit torque-induced effective magnetic field on a magnetization

squareness.description: A parameter indicating how close the shape of the hysteresis curve is to a square

total shielding effectiveness.description: amount of the shielded electromagnetic waves from the material

work function.description: minimum thermodynamic work (i.e., energy) needed to remove an electron from a solid to a point in the vacuum immediately outside the solid surface

mechanical property.description: physical properties that a material exhibits upon the application of forces

compressive property.description: properties indicate how the material will react to forces being applied in compression

compressive fracture strain.description: maximum deformation or strain a material can undergo in compression when it fails or fractures completely

compressive fracture strength.description: maximum stress or force per unit area that a material can withstand under compression when it fails or fractures completely

compressive modulus.description: ratio of stress to strain in elastic region under compression

compressive yield strength.description: yield strength of material during compressive test

ultimate compressive strength.description: maximum compressive strength of material during compressive test

creep property.description: materials response upon long-term exposure to high levels of stress that are still below the yield strength of the materials

0.2% creep strain time.description: time required to reach 0.2% strain during a creep test

creep compliance.description: a measure of the deformation of a material under a constant stress over time

creep rupture strain.description: total strain after creep rupture test

creep rupture strength.description: stress causing fracture in a creep test at a given time, in a specified constant environment

instantaneous strain.description: immediate deformation of materials upon initial application of a stress

minimum creep rate.description: slope of the portion of the creep vs. time diagram corresponding to secondary creep

reduction of area.description: proportional reduction of the cross-sectional area of a creep test piece at the plane of fracture measured after fracture

rupture time.description: time necessary produce failure while materials is subjected to constant load at a constant temperature

stress exponent.description: value of a stress exponent, n, obtained via creep rate measurements over a range of applied stress

time to tertiary creep.description: time necessary to reach tertiary creep stage

elastic property.description: mechanical property of a material to withstand the compression or the elongation with respect to its length

bulk modulus.description: measure of how resistant to compression that substance is

elastic recovery ratio.description: ability to recover elastically after the removal of the elastic load in nano indentation; it is defined as the ratio of elastic recovery displacement (the amount of deformation recovered after the load is removed) to the maximum indentation depth during loading

Poisson's ratio.description: ratio of transverse strain to corresponding axial strain on a material stressed along one axis

resilience modulus.description: measure of resilience modulus defined as the maximum energy that can be absorbed per unit volume without creating permanent distortion

Young's modulus.description: elastic properties of materials undergoing tension or compression in one direction

fatigue property.description: materials response when subjected to cyclic load and/or strain

fatigue type.description: type of fatigue properties depending on number of cycles, applied stress and/or strain level and environment

fatigue life.description: number of stress (strain) cycles required to cause failure

fatigue limit.description: highest stress that materials can withstand for an infinite number of cycles without breaking

fatigue crack growth rate.description: rate of crack extension under fatigue loading, expressed in terms of crack extension per cycle, da/dN

stress intensity factor.description: magnitude of the mathematically ideal, crack-tip stress field for a particular mode in a homogeneous, linear-elastic body

stress intensity factor range.description: variation in the stress intensity factor in a cycle in fatigue

fatigue crack growth threshold.description: asymptotic value of stress intensity factor range at which crack growth rate approaches zero

flexural property.description: properties indicate how the material will react to forces being applied in bending

flexural modulus.description: ratio of stress to strain in elastic region in flexural deformation

flexural yield stress.description: stress in a material just before it yields in a flexure test

flexural strength.description: stress in a material at the exact moment the specimen fractures (snaps)

fracture toughness.description: generic term for measures of resistance to extension of a crack

stress intensity factor.description: magnitude of the mathematically ideal, crack-tip stress field for a particular mode in a homogeneous, linear-elastic body

plane strain fracture toughness K.description: crack-extension resistance under conditions of crack-tip plane strain in mode I and predominantly linear-elastic conditions

plane strain fracture toughness J.description: crack-extension resistance under conditions of crack-tip plane strain in mode I and substantial plastic deformation

crack tip opening displacement.description: crack displacement resulting from the total deformation at variously defined locations near the original crack tip

hardness.description: measure of the resistance to localized plastic deformation induced by either mechanical indentation or abrasion

impact toughness.description: toughness of a material using the value of impact energy absorbed by the maerial during fracturing under impact

ductile-to-brittle transition temperatur.description: temperature at which there is a pronounced decrease in a material’s ability to absorb force without fracturing

impact energy.description: work done to fracture a test specimen measured by Charpy impact test

impact strength.description: amount of energy absorbed per unit cross-sectional aera of a specimen during fracture by impact loading

upper shelf energy.description: high fracture energy associated with ductile behavior

lower shelf energy.description: low fracture energy associated with brittle behavior

residual stress.description: internal stress locked within a solid material after the original external force is removed; the stress that remains in a material or thin film after fabrication, deposition, or processing, in the absence of external forces or loads; it can be either tensile (+) or compressive (-)

shear property.description: properties indicate how the material will react to forces being applied in shear

shear modulus.description: ratio of shear stress to the shear strain

shear yield strength.description: shear stress at which plastic deformation begins, corresponding to the elastic-to-plastic transition under shear loading

ultimate shear strength.description: maximum shear stress a material can sustain, corresponding to the peak of the engineering shear stress-strain curve

fracture shear strength.description: shear stress at which fracture occurs, corresponding to the final failure point under shear loading

sheet metal formability.description: ease with which a sheet metal can be shaped through plastic deformation

plastic strain ratio.description: ratio of true plastic width strain to the true plastic thickness strain in a tensile test

normal anisotropy.description: ratio of the logarithmic strain in the transverse direction (TD) to the logarithmic strain in the normal direction (ND)

planar anisotropy.description: variation of plastic strain ratio with direction in the plane of the sheet

limiting drawing ratio.description: ratio of the maximum blank diameter that can be drawn into a cup without failure, to the diameter of the punch

bendability.description: ability of a material to be bent around a specified radius without fracture

hole expansion ratio.description: ratio of the expanded hole diameter to the initial hole diameter

springback ratio.description: ratio of the radius of curvature after springback to the radius at the end of forming

tensile property.description: properties indicate how the material will react to forces being applied in tension

critical resolved shear stress.description: the minimum resolved shear stress required along a specific crystal direction on a specific crystal plane to initiate plastic mechanisms such as dislocation slip or twinning

fracture strength.description: maximum stress or force per unit area that a material can withstand under tensile condition when it fails or fractures completely

reduction of area.description: proportional reduction of the cross-sectional area of a tensile test piece at the plane of fracture measured after fracture

specific strength.description: strength normalized by material density (strength-to-weight ratio)

strain hardening exponent.description: constant used in calculations relating to stress-strain bahavior in work hardening

tensile toughness.description: amount of energy a material can absorb before it fractures characterized from the area under the stress-strain curve

total elongation.description: percentage by which the material can be stretched before it breaks

ultimate tensile strength.description: maximum stress that can be applied to the material before it breaks
ultimate tensile strength.alias: ultimate tensile stress; UTS; R_m; tensile strength

uniform elongation.description: elongation at maximum load and immediately preceding the onset of necking in a tensile test

yield strength.description: stress value at which the plastic deformation of a material begins to occur
yield strength.alias: yield stress; YS; R_{p0.2}; tensile yield strength

absorption.description: process by which matter takes up photons of light energy, resulting in a transition of electrons from lower to higher energy states

first peak position.description: first peak observed in the absorption spectrum
first peak position.alias: exciton absorption peak; absorption peak; first excitonic peak; first exciton peak

peak to valley.description: ratio of the maximum peak to the valley signal in a response curve, typically used to evaluate the sharpness or contrast of optical or electronic signals

half width at half maximum.description: distance between the center of a peak and the point at which the intensity is half of the peak value

cutoff wavelength.description: wavelength beyond which an optical material or system no longer transmits, detects, or supports propagation effectively

optical bandgap.description: optical band gap obtained from the absorption spectrum

absorbance.description: quantity of light absorbed by an object, defined as the logarithm of the ratio of incident to transmitted or reflected radiation power through a material

absorption coefficient.description: a value representing how far into a material light of a particular wavelength can penetrate before it is absorbed

electroluminescence.description: light emission in response to the passage of an electric current or to a strong electric field

lifetime.description: emissive decays time from the excited state

quantum efficiency.description: number of photons emitted per injected electrons

peak position.description: a wavelength where the intensity of electroluminescence reaches its maximum value; If more than one peak positions, separate those by comma

haze.description: amount of light that is scattered away from the direct optical path when passing through a transparent material. It is typically measured as the percentage of light that deviates by more than 2.5 degrees from the incident beam.

photoluminescence.description: light emission from any form of matter after the absorption of photons

luminescence type.description: type of emission through photoexcitation; Luminescence is classified according to the magnitude of the delay time between absorption and reemission events. If reemission occurs for times much less than 1 s, the phenomenon is termed fluorescence. If reemission occurs for longer than 1 second, the phenomenon is termed phosphorescence.

lifetime.description: emissive decays time from the excited state

quantum efficiency.description: number of photons emitted per absorbed photons of excitation source

peak position.description: a wavelength where the intensity of photoluminescence reaches its maximum value; If more than one peak positions, separate those by comma

full width at half maximum.description: width of a peak measured between the two points on the curve where the intensity falls to half of the peak maximum

quantum yield.description: ratio of the number of photons emitted to the number of photons absorbed by a material

maximum peak wavelength.description: wavelength at which a substance absorbs the maximum amount of ultraviolet light
maximum peak wavelength.alias: maximum absorption wavelength; UV absorbance peak

reflectance.description: ratio of the radiation flux reflected by a sample surface to the incident radiation flux

transmittance.description: ratio of light that is transmitted through a material to the total incident light

normal incidence transmittance.description: ratio of the radiation flux normally transmitted through a sample to the incident radiation flux

yellowness index.description: a measure of how much a material has changed color from clear or white towards yellow. It is calculated from spectrophotometric data using the CIE Tristimulus values (ASTM E313 or ASTM D1925).

CIE tristimulus value.description: adapted CIE values for yellow index

dispersion.description: change in refractive index as a function of wavelength

dispersion data.description: ratio of the speed of the light in the vacuum to that in a material for each wavelength of incidence light

abbe number.description: a measure of a material’s optical dispersion, defined as the ratio that indicates how much the refractive index of the material changes with wavelength

refractive index.description: ratio of the speed of the light in the vacuum to that in a material

photorecombination rate.description: rate of recombination of two particles and the excess energy from the reaction is released in the form of a photon (a particle of light)

trap-assisted recombination.description: rate of recombination between electrons and holes through trap states within the bandgap

bimolecular recombination.description: rate of recombination between free electrons and holes through direct two-body interaction

auger recombination.description: recombination rate at which energy is transferred to other carriers

oxidation property.description: properties related to oxidation of a material as it reacts with oxygen

weight change.description: variation in the weight of a specimen as a result of exposure to an oxidizing environment at elevated temperatures

surface morphology.description: surface morphology after the oxidation test

oxide layer thickness.description: thickness of the continuous oxide scale layer that forms on the surface of a material as a result of exposure to an oxidizing environment at elevated temperatures

diffusion layer thickness.description: thickness of the diffusion layer formed by interdiffusion between the oxide scale and the metallic matrix during the oxidation test

oxidation rate.description: speed at which a material reacts with oxygen

metal loss.description: reduction in the thickness of base metal due to its consumption during oxidation

piezoelectric property.description: property of certain materials which induces an electric field when mechanical stress is applied OR VICE VERSA

piezoelectric strain coefficient.description: strain induced when polarized when electric field applied, presented by values assigned to symbols d*_{ij}, i.e. d*_{11}, d*_{22}, d*_{33} etc.

piezoelectric voltage coefficient.description: voltage induced when polarized when stress applied, presented by values assigned to symbols g_{ij}, i.e. g_{11}, g_{22}, g_{33} etc.

piezoelectric charge coefficient.description: electrical charge induced when polarized when stress is applied, presented by values assigned to symbols d_{ij}, i.e. d_{11}, d_{22}, d_{33} etc.

electromechanical coupling factor.description: conversion efficiency between electrical and mechanical energy,k^2

mechanical quality factor.description: Variables that indicate how little loss is in piezoelectric deformation (It is the inverse of the mechanical loss tan ϕ)

radiation resistance.description: observed changes in mechanical, physical, and microstructural properties of the material after irradiation

irradiated hardness.description: Vickers hardness of the specimen measured after irradiation

irradiated yield strength.description: yield strength of the specimen measured after irradiation.

irradiated elongation.description: total elongation of the specimen after irradiation.

DBTT shift.description: change in ductile-to-brittle transition temperature (DBTT) induced by irradiation.

irradiation creep rate.description: steady-state rate of deformation under irradiation.

lattice parameter change.description: variation in the lattice parameter determined from X-ray diffraction (XRD).

peak shift.description: change in XRD peak position after irradiation.

defect loop density.description: areal density of irradiation-induced dislocation loops (e.g., self-interstitial atom loops).

stacking fault tetrahedra density.description: number density of stacking fault tetrahedra formed due to irradiation.

average void diameter.description: mean diameter of voids formed during irradiation.

phase fraction change.description: change in the fraction of the HCP phase after irradiation, relevant to the phase stability of HEAs.

rheological property.description: material properties that govern the specific way in which materials deform or flowing response to applied forces or stresses

viscosity.description: resistance of a fluid (liquid or gas) to a change in shape, or movement of neighboring portions relative to one another; Viscosity is dependent on temperature, shear rate and time of measurement. Required items of the array data are to be selected, depending on the control parameter of the measurement.

temperature.description: temperature at which rheological properties are characterised

shear rate.description: shear rate applied for rheological property measurement

duration.description: time during which rheological properties are characterized

absolute viscosity.description: internal friction force gnenerated when a fluid flows; the ratio of shear stres to shear rate when fluid layers slide past each other

relative viscosity.description: ratio of the viscosity of the polymer sotuion to the viscosity of the pure solvent

specific viscosity.description: relative fractional increase in viscosity caused by dissolving the polymer in the pure solvent; (specific viscosity) = (relative viscosity)-1

inherent viscosity.description: equal to ln{(relative viscosity)} divided by mass concentration of polymer; it is synonymous with the logarithmic viscosity number, expressed conventionally in mL g^{-1}

intrinsic viscosity.description: reduced viscosity in infinite dilute solution of the polymer or limit of the value of inherent viscosity

reduced viscosity.description: specific viscosity value adjusted to account for the effects of concentration; the ratio of the specific viscosity of a polymer solution to its concentration

viscoelasticity.description: response of fluid (slurry or liquid) resistance to a change in shape, or movement of neighboring portions relative to one another by shear rate

loss tangent.description: ratio of loss modulus to storage modulus, indicating the viscoelastic balance of a material

yield strength.description: stress at which a polymer material transitions from elastic deformation — where strain is reversible — to plastic deformation, where permanent molecular rearrangement begins.

stress relaxation time.description: time it takes for a material to relax its internal stresses when a constant strain is applied. It is a measure of how quickly the material can dissipate the applied stress over time.

surface property.description: properties to characterize the surface of materials

surface energy.description: excess free energy per unit area required to create a surface of a material or a surface model

contact angle.description: angle formed between a liquid droplet and a solid surface, indicating surface wettability

RMS surface roughness.description: root mean square value (RMS) of the surface roughness expressed in nm (mapping: Perovskite DB 5.4); the irregularities or deviations in the texture of a surface, typically at a micro or nanoscale level. It quantifies the variations in height of the surface features from the ideal smooth surface.”

thermoelectric property.description: materials property that can either convert directly heat into electricity or convert an electrical power into a cooling source; The materials properties are composed of Seebeck coefficient, power factor and ZT value, which are dependent on the temperature
